definition: Implied heat rate (also called market implied heat rate or implied market heat rate) is the ratio of power price to fuel price — expressed in the same MMBtu/MWh units as a plant's physical heat rate — computed either as current power price over current fuel price, or as average power price over average natural gas price in a given market on a given day, the latter used to express the generation stack in heat-rate terms instead of dollar terms.
core_idea: Dividing the power price by the fuel price restates the price relationship in heat-rate units, letting it be compared directly to plant heat rates or used to infer how much of a power price move is explained by fuel prices versus a shift in the generation stack.
key_points: Because comparing power-to-fuel price ratios against plant heat rates is so common, this ratio is given its own name.
Same units (MMBtu/MWh) as a physical plant heat rate, enabling direct comparison across plant efficiencies.

Auction bids and load producers' break-even costs are not publicly disclosed (bids are private, and generation-stack composition is only released years later by the ISO/RTO), so historical prices and heat rates are used to estimate the stack instead.
A generation stack can be expressed either as prices or as heat rates by dividing prices by the day's natural gas price.
If implied heat rates stay unchanged between two periods, the price ratio between power and gas is constant, meaning the fuel-price change fully explains the power-price change.

In the source's August 2005 example, natural gas rose from $8.02 to $12.70/MMBtu alongside a large power price increase, but on the portion of the stack where gas was the marginal fuel, market heat rates barely changed between the two days (Figures 4.2.8-4.2.9) — indicating the gas price move, not a stack shift, explained the power price move on that segment.
relationships: Compared directly against a plant's physical heat rate to judge which plant efficiencies are currently profitable.
Connects to generation stack and marginal-fuel bidding for fuel-dependent producers.
trading_implications: Traders track market implied heat rate by region to see which plant efficiency classes are economic to dispatch in that region.
Implied heat rate is a diagnostic for decomposing a power price move into a fuel-price-driven component vs. a generation-stack-shift component.
Useful for estimating/predicting power prices from historical price relationships and current fuel prices, given that actual auction bids and plant economics are not public.
caveats: Because actual auction bids and generation-stack composition are not publicly disclosed at the time (stack composition is released by the ISO/RTO only years later), implied heat rate is an estimate derived from historical prices, not a direct observation of the stack.

versions.statement: Market Implied Heat Rate = Power Price / Fuel Price (current power price over current fuel price, generic fuel)
Implied Heat Rate = Average Power Price / Average Natural Gas Price, computed in a given market on a given day

contradictions.note: One item defines the ratio using current/point-in-time power and (generic) fuel prices; the other specifies daily-average power and natural-gas prices for a given market. Not resolved into a single formula since the items differ on both the price convention (current vs. daily average) and fuel specificity (generic fuel vs. natural gas).

formulas.name: Market implied heat rate
formulas.formula: Market Implied Heat Rate = Power Price / Fuel Price

variables.Fuel Price: current market price of fuel (e.g., natural gas)

formulas.name: Implied Market Heat Rate
formulas.formula: Implied Heat Rate = Average Power Price / Average Natural Gas Price

variables.Average Power Price: $/MWh, average power price in a specific geographic market over a period (e.g., a day)
variables.Average Natural Gas Price: $/MMBtu, average natural gas price in the same market/period
